tasks.subject: fix(subagent): share Cargo build output per checkout (#3)
tasks.brief: Subagent children that build Rust code should share build output per checkout. Provide agent/extensions/subagent/build-env.ts exporting cargoEnvDefaults(cwd, env), which returns the Cargo environment defaults to apply. With PI_CARGO_TARGET_ROOT unset, the only default is { CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0" }. With it set, also return CARGO_TARGET_DIR under that root, named <checkout folder name>-<hash of the git checkout root>: stable for every working directory inside one checkout, distinct between two checkouts (including one whose .git is a file), and with a hash that preserves path case on case-sensitive platforms. A directory with no git checkout root gets no CARGO_TARGET_DIR default. Values already present in env (CARGO_TARGET_DIR, CARGO_INCREMENTAL) always win: nothing is returned for them. Apply the defaults when a child process is launched and document PI_CARGO_TARGET_ROOT in agent/AGENTS.md.
tasks.riskRationale: New build-env module and wiring in index and code-integrations; the held-out test imports a module the parent lacks, so RED is a missing-module failure.

tasks.subject: fix(subagent): preserve literal Sonnet 5.5 routing (#5)
tasks.brief: Model fallback routing must keep literal model identifiers exactly as configured. In agent/extensions/subagent/model-routing.ts: parseFallbackModels splits a '||' separated fallback string into an ordered, trimmed, de-duplicated list that keeps every id verbatim (for example anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5, github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5, openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol); getFallbackSequence(primary, fallbacks) drops only an exact match of the primary; nextFallbackModel(result, chain) returns the next chain entry only for an availability or provider failure (for example a 503 unavailable error) and never after a task failure message, an aborted stop or any tool activity; shouldRetryWithFallback(result, primary, fallback) is true for a quota or usage-limit failure with no tool activity and false once tools ran (edits could replay), after cancelled work, or for a task failure. Find every place in the launch path, role registry, role prompts, docs and roles.json that rewrites, normalises or loses these literals, and make the declared primary and ordered fallbacks reach the child launch unchanged.
tasks.riskRationale: Routing literals guarded by model-routing and fallback-runtime tests; a wrong literal changes which model a role launches. The fallback-runtime wrapper launches the .node.ts suite, so that suite is held out too.

tasks.subject: fix(harness): harden retirement policy and recorded tier scoring
tasks.brief: Harden the post-merge cleanup and worktree retirement policy text so each rule is explicit and testable. Routine post-merge cleanup removes exactly three named task-owned targets and never bulk-copies, archives, sweeps or forces; it waits for the knowledge checkpoint (a BLOCKED checkpoint retains the target and never rolls back a merge); keeps temp, log and report destinations outside every deletion target; retains any target with unique or unreproduced required evidence, user data, or an active, paused, service, database, shared, unauthorized or unmerged state, with a concrete reason; and verifies shared publication from a freshly fetched base by blob id, never by squash-prone commit ancestry. A separate explicit retirement mode needs user-disposition authority naming each exact path and operation; discarding a dirty checkout needs explicit discard consent that a merge or general cleanup never implies; it force-removes only the listed discarded checkouts and then the exact approved parent, rejects active, primary, live-database and unknown-owner targets, keeps artifacts and reports outside targets, and runs in the order preflight, knowledge, checkouts, registrations, parent, verification. Routine cleanup keeps its ordinary ban and stays separate from retirement. SHIP, AGENTS and the README point to retirement without granting authority. The release-engineer prompt mirrors the three-target cleanup, keeps arbitrary directory deletion forbidden, and states that named write paths are instruction-enforced rather than hard filesystem isolation. Legacy guide.md files remain tiny pointers to the same-folder index.md. Keep the routing evaluator's recorded-tier scoring consistent with the updated policy.
tasks.riskRationale: Retirement policy and tier scoring span the role registry, prompts and routing evaluation; a wrong policy can retire active roles. Acceptance is the Bun suite role-prompt-dedup; the registry suite is declared but not run (its GREEN depends on the installed model catalog). The Python evaluator test is declared but not run.

tasks.subject: feat(subagent): relay worker decisions and inspect monitor (#6)
tasks.brief: Let a background worker ask the main session for a decision without hanging, and let the operator see what workers are doing. Add a pure registry module decision-relay-state.ts (class DecisionRelay, parseDecisionRequest) and a worker-side extension decision-relay.ts that registers a request_decision tool only when the parent relay environment is set and a UI exists. A request is strict and bounded: unknown keys, blank or over-long fields (question over 1000 characters), more than six options, blank options and malformed ids are rejected; a free-form question without options is valid; ids are unique, a worker has at most one open request and a session at most four. The worker announces the request, then opens one exact input dialog titled for that request; only that exact dialog is held for the main, every other dialog keeps the automatic cancel. The main is notified once through a subagent-decision message and can list requests with subagent_control action "decisions", answer (with basis and reference) or decline. An answer is accepted only while the request is open and is recorded only after the write to the worker is confirmed; blank, mismatched, late, duplicate or unbased answers are errors; settlement is exactly once and scoped to that worker and job, and cancel, job end, worker exit, session reset or a failed or closed stdin settle the request as not answered without hanging or unhandled errors. Answering a paused job never resumes it, and an unrelated job keeps running meanwhile. Background spawns grant a worker only the request_decision addition to its allow-list; foreground runs get nothing extra.
tasks.riskRationale: New decision-relay state and runtime relay between workers and the main session. Acceptance is decision-relay only; monitor-scrollbar.test.ts is declared but not held out because it needs the absent Pi TUI install.

tasks.subject: fix(harness): stabilize delegation and reuse PR push approval
tasks.brief: Stabilise delegation and let an approved release-engineer reuse one session-scoped push lease instead of needing a fresh single-use approval for each push. In the safety core: validatePushBranch accepts ordinary feature branch names and refuses protected, unsafe, non-ASCII, tag-like and releases-family names; parseNormalPush accepts exactly three whole-command push forms and treats every other push shape as not a normal push; a child holding a lease may run the exact normal push in bash and PowerShell repeatedly (the lease is not consumed) while every other push shape stays blocked; a lease is bound to a verified repository with exactly one origin push URL and refuses on drift, extra push URLs, mirror, followTags, receive-pack settings, submodule recursion, a tag named like the branch, URLs that embed login data, a subdirectory or a missing branch; copies of the lease reach first, fallback and later spawns of the right role only, abort keeps approved leases while an explicit revoke clears them, and tampered or old-format envelopes fail closed. A job's first spawn closes the grant-claim window so a later fallback spawn claims no late grant. Shell and path classification also covers glued and spaced redirections (including >| and >&), escaped operators, 8.3 short names and Pi path forms, with ordinary quoted text and real pipes left unflagged and grants staying exact.
tasks.riskRationale: Delegation stability and PR push approval reuse touch the safety core and the delivery approval path; a wrong approval reuse is a release-safety defect. Acceptance is safety-core (50 tests); workspace-admission expects a real git checkout root and is declared but not held out.

tasks.subject: Save learned lessons as focused Markdown records
tasks.brief: Implement the harness feature that turns a verified lesson into a focused Markdown knowledge record. This task changes only harness prompt, module and documentation text and saves no real knowledge. package.json exports only the prompt template ./agent/prompts/learn.md, which has front matter with a description, passes $ARGUMENTS, resolves the advertised engineering-harness SKILL.md without any hard-coded home-directory path and loads learn/index.md, names the three outcomes SAVED, NO LESSON and BLOCKED and allows SAVED only after the destination is verified, dedupes with qmd_search (at most 5 results, collections knowledge-general and knowledge-harness, a file-search fallback, no index refresh), and dispatches release-engineer in the foreground (background false) with candidate, evidence, destination, scope and checks plus an absolute module path, allowing a new document only with explicit authority. The learn module records the fields Title, claim, Source, Evidence status, Context and date and Revalidate when as set out in docs/knowledge/README.md; defines a trigger of three distinct incidents with a confirmed shared root cause and REPORT evidence, driven by evidence (no history scan, counter, ledger or background pipeline, and three is not a minimum); keeps one small focused record per lesson with the README as a link index, exact record and index authority and a readback before SAVED; updates the existing canonical record when a claim repeats; and never substitutes for a root-cause fix. The release-engineer may write only the named knowledge or release artifacts, never a shell or product bypass.
tasks.riskRationale: Learned-lessons record format and learn prompt. Acceptance is the Bun suite learn-prompt; safety-config-scan needs an installed pi-coding-agent package and is declared but not held out.

tasks.subject: docs(harness): consolidate guides and add opt-in compaction safeguards
tasks.brief: Add opt-in compaction safeguards and consolidate the guides. In compact-handoff.ts export BACKGROUND_COMPLETION_LIMIT (4000), COMPACT_HANDOFF_INSTRUCTIONS, boundBackgroundCompletion(text, jobId), expandRetainedResult, extractFinalText, retainedEntryBlock and withTerminalDiagnostics. A background completion at or under the limit is delivered unchanged; an oversized one stays within 4000 code units (never splitting a surrogate pair), is marked INCOMPLETE HANDOFF, carries the exact recovery command subagent_control action "result" target "<job>", keeps a head excerpt and the priority STATUS, RISKS and ERROR verdict lines, and never claims PASS. extractFinalText joins every text block of the last meaningful assistant message (skipping tool-call-only or blank tails); expandRetainedResult returns the full child report, labels exit 0 without a terminal stop as INCOMPLETE, reports failed or aborted children as failures with exact error text, joins parallel and chain steps in order, and appends a terminal diagnostic only when it is not already carried as a canonical block. Guidance names every handoff field and states that exit 0 is not PASS. Also provide external-compaction-entry.ts exporting registerExternalCompaction(pi, { env }): with PI_EXTERNAL_COMPACTION not exactly "1" it registers nothing; opted in it registers only session_start (one info note naming PI_EXTERNAL_COMPACTION=1) and session_before_compact, which cancels manual compaction with a warning that an external proxy owns compression, and cancels threshold and overflow compaction silently or with a warning (never retried), without UI notification in child mode.
tasks.riskRationale: Opt-in compaction safeguards and external compaction entry: this is the compaction behaviour the benchmark exists to measure. Acceptance is the held-out node suites compact-handoff and external-compaction; Bun suites and the runtime suite are declared but not held out.

tasks.subject: Release v1.9.1
tasks.brief: Implement delivery safety in the harness guard so that a merge approval is bound to the exact verified candidate; this task changes guard code, tests and documentation only and performs no real merge, release, push or publication. Add candidate-fingerprint.ts with a deterministic, typed and bounded fingerprint of a candidate checkout covering HEAD, branch, staged, unstaged and untracked content, where ignored files, ref updates, upstream changes and excluded output do not invalidate it. bindDelivery refuses a detached HEAD, another branch, UNSUPPORTED entries, tracked or malformed excludes and a mismatch with the expected fingerprint; repository-local git filters or config are never executed, links and junctions are never traversed, and index flags that hide edits (assume-unchanged, skip-worktree, sparse checkout) fail closed. A merge grant carries its bound state (head, ref, fingerprint, excludes) under a separate envelope key, is refused after any change to the candidate, requires the merge to match the bound HEAD commit, and a newer bound state replaces only the older bound record; unbound grants behave exactly as before and status output labels bound grants honestly. PR workflow authorisation stays narrow: an ordinary trusted commit (message or quoted file form), a feature push and PR creation need no grant; a merge or release creation needs an explicit grant of its own that push or commit leases never cover; the origin repository-name artifact group is accepted next to the legacy group while traversal, wrong extension, embedded login data and oversize files are refused; an unsupported commit form gets one fixed hint that leaks nothing.
tasks.riskRationale: Delivery candidate fingerprint, grant and PR workflow authorisation: a wrong binding lets an unreviewed candidate ship. Acceptance is the held-out node suites for delivery-bound, delivery-grant, pr-workflow-auth and safety-core; Bun suites and the delivery runtime are declared but not held out.
